Whether the expiration a read-back carries is reached on the day of a round

mail_expiration_reached.Rd

The stored expiration is the day after the last day of access, so it is reached when it is not later than the day of the round: REDCap, whose server runs UTC, denies access when expiration <= TODAY. The day is the UTC one of at, not the clock of whoever composes the message, so the same row says the same thing whenever it is read and the tests do not depend on the machine. validate_request() and the choice of lapsed read the date of the machine (Sys.Date()), which is the same day on a machine in UTC; on one in another zone the two differ between the midnights, and the message then says "granted" for that stretch, as the limit of the gate on the last day already does.

Usage

mail_expiration_reached(applied_as, at)

Arguments

applied_as

The row's read-back, role_name=...; dag_name=...; expiration=....

at

The time of the round, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M" in UTC.

Value

TRUE when both carry a date and the expiration is not later than the day of at; FALSE otherwise, which is the answer for every row that says nothing readable.
